narration.full_text: Namaste, students! Welcome to our final quiz on Control and Coordination. This section will test your understanding of how living organisms regulate their activities and respond to stimuli. Let's dive right in! First question: Write names of hormones secreted by the pituitary gland and adrenal gland. State their functions in the body. And explain the feedback mechanism for regulation of hormonal secretion with the help of one example. Take a moment to think about this comprehensive question. The pituitary gland secretes growth hormone, which regulates the growth and development of the body. The adrenal gland secretes adrenaline hormone, which creates stress in our body. The timing and amount of hormones released by various glands are controlled by a feedback mechanism. For example, if the sugar level in blood rises too high, it's detected by cells of the pancreas, which respond by producing and secreting more insulin into the blood. As blood sugar falls to a certain level, the secretion of insulin is reduced automatically. Next question: What happens at the synapse between two neurons? Pause and recall the process of nerve impulse transmission. At the synapse, the electrical impulse generated at the dendrites of a neuron is passed on to the dendrite of another neuron in the form of chemicals by the axon ending of the first neuron. Moving on: Design an experiment to demonstrate hydrotropism. Think about how plants respond to water. Hydrotropism can be demonstrated with any germinating seedlings allowed to grow on the ground. The soil around the roots is separated by a polythene partition. The left side is kept moist and the right side dry. The radicle at first grows downward, and after some time, the roots bend towards the moist soil. This is due to the movement of the germinating roots towards water. And finally: Why is the use of iodized salt advisable? Consider the role of iodine in our body. Iodine is necessary to make thyroxine hormone, which regulates carbohydrate, protein, and fat metabolism in the body to provide the best balance for growth. Great job, everyone! This quiz covered some key concepts in control and coordination. Keep revising these important topics!
